column1: #mapping_set_title: CALM to OCSF (Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework) class mappings

#mapping_set_description: Schema-level mappings between the FINOS Common Architecture Language Model (CALM 1.2) and the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) LinkML schema. OCSF's objects.yaml defines Node, Actor, Compliance, Evidences, NetworkInterface, and NetworkTraffic - these align closely with CALM's architecture primitives. CALM Node maps to both OCSF Node and Actor; CALM Control maps to OCSF Compliance; CALM EvidenceDocument maps to OCSF Evidences; CALM Flow maps to NetworkTraffic.

column7: CALM Node and OCSF Node are both named structural elements representing infrastructure or logical components in a system - the concepts align directly, with OCSF Node specifically modelling endpoint and infrastructure elements.

When a CALM Node is typed as a human or service actor (e.g. actor node-type), it aligns with OCSF Actor which represents the entity performing an action - the actor sub-role of CALM Node maps closely to OCSF Actor.

A CALM Control specifies a domain-scoped security requirement on an architecture element; OCSF Compliance captures compliance check results including the control mapping - both represent the compliance status of a controlled element.

A CALM EvidenceDocument links evidence artefacts to a control configuration URL; OCSF Evidences is a structured container for evidence data objects in security events - both package evidence related to a security control or finding.

A CALM InterfaceDefinition specifies a named interface on a node (with host, port, protocol); OCSF NetworkInterface captures the same network interface properties - both model a bounded network attachment point on a component.

A CALM Flow describes a business process traversing nodes and relationships via a sequence of transitions; OCSF NetworkTraffic models the network packets and sessions traversing a network - related as both trace end-to-end traversal of a system.

A CALM Relationship is a typed directed link between two CALM Nodes; OCSF NetworkEndpoint represents the source or destination in a network interaction - related in that both model a directed connectivity between components.
